output.name: Ketha
output.myth: When the first frost comes to the islands, the stew-pots come in from the yard and go up on the hook, and that is why Ketha rises then. Ennu bent it first from a rib of old whale, so the pot would hang over the fire and not in the wind. Aun saw it from the cliff and wanted it for his own. He took it down to the Upper Sea to cook a fish too big for the islands, and the pot went with him, and the hook on its string. Hesk counted the pots that night and found one short. Tavo laughed and blew the pot away over the water. The hook stayed in the sky with its tip still empty, waiting. Grandmothers say a kettle must always be hung again. Mind your own pots, and you will not need Aun to mend them.
output.verse:
Hook in the cold dark,
the stew-pot waits for its fire,
Frost brings the pot back.
